evidence.quote: If the city council agrees later this month and extends the data center moratorium until next March, it will allow city officials to see what plays out in either the state government's veto session

decisions.notes: EXTENDED_NO_END_DATE: confirmed the extension ordinance (2026-57) was scheduled for a Sept. 21, 2026 Council vote (two days before this research pass), but minutes/confirmation of that vote were not yet posted to the city's AgendaCenter as of 2026-09-23, and the only reported target end date ('until next March') is not a specific calendar date. Row left unchanged pending posted minutes or news confirming the vote and an exact end date.

current_end_date_iso.reason: EXTENDED_NO_END_DATE: Shaw Local News Network reports the City Council's Aug. 18/19, 2026 unanimous vote extended the moratorium through a specific date.

evidence.title: Robinson solar farm moratorium extended
evidence.supports: Confirms a further six-month extension of the solar-farm moratorium was voted by the City Council, but gives no vote date, ordinance number, or resulting end date.

decisions.notes: EXTENDED_NO_END_DATE: both located news articles describe the moratorium and its rolling extensions only in general terms (no vote date, ordinance number, or specific new end date given), consistent with the row's own pre-existing [VERIFY] marker. evidence.title: Tazewell County revisits data center ordinance; Woodford County passes moratorium
evidence.supports: Full account of the Woodford County Board's action: the moratorium adopted covers only 'data center applications.' A board member's supporting statement separately references the county's past approach to 'wind and solar projects' as a point of comparison for how carefully to proceed, not as part of the moratorium's operative scope.
evidence.quote: the County Board approved a six-month moratorium on data center applications, with an option for a six-month extension... He said the county should approach the issue diligently, as it has with other large developments, including wind and solar projects.

decisions.notes: SECTOR_CHECK (solar, wind): both mentions of solar/wind in the sourced reporting are a board member's comparison to how the county previously regulated those sectors, not language describing the moratorium's own scope, which is limited to 'data center applications.' Per the process rule, such a comparison/trigger mention does not count, so sectors correctly remains ["data_center"].
